post.description:
Rotate a refresh token into a new pair.

Reuse detection: if the presented token was already rotated or revoked, the
whole family is revoked (the token leaked, so none of them can be trusted)
and the caller gets ``401 refresh_token_reused``.

Turn the anonymous caller into a registered account, keeping all data.

The user id never changes, so chat sessions, journal entries, mood entries
and consents stay attached. Every existing refresh token is revoked — an
identity change signs everything out — and one fresh pair is returned.

Assess one message: rules engine + ML ensemble, then the response plan.

The matchers are CPU-bound and synchronous, so they run in a thread pool
rather than blocking the event loop. The assessment and the plan are pure
metadata plus pre-written copy: nothing derived from the input text is
echoed back. At MEDIUM or above a metadata-only ``safety_events`` row is
written (level + source, never text).

post.description:
Record one check-in; screen the optional note before storing it.

The order is deliberate: **screen, then store**. A note that needs help is
still stored, together with a metadata-only audit row. A note we could not
screen is not stored at all, because the alternative is silently keeping
somebody's worst sentence with nobody told to look at it.

A ``client_id`` that is already stored is a replay (Day 25): it is screened
like any other request — so a lost first answer cannot lose the helplines —
but nothing new is written and the answer is ``200`` with ``replayed: true``.

get.description:
The streak, counted in the caller's timezone with forgiving rules.

Read the module docstring of :mod:`app.services.mood.streak` before changing
anything here. The short version: today is still open, one missed day in
seven is bridged, and coming back after a gap is "welcome back" — never a
number that was taken away.

Every check is reported in ``checks``; the probe fails closed with 503 when
any of them fails, so an orchestrator never routes traffic to a process that
cannot persist data. Only the outcome is exposed — never a DSN, a driver
error, or any other detail that could describe the deployment.
